+\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic denominator-layer theorem]
+\label{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
+For a finite word \(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\) of positive integers, let
+\(\mathcal K(\mathbf a)\) be its regular continuant, with
+\[
+ \begin{gathered}
+  \mathcal K(\varnothing)=1,\qquad \mathcal K(a_1)=a_1,\\
+  \mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)
+  =a_r\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1})
+   +\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-2}).
+ \end{gathered}
+\]
+Put
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+  \mathcal L&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
+   \bigcup_{r\ge1}\mathbb N^r,\\
+  \mathcal R&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
+   \{(a_1,\ldots,a_r):r\ge1,\ a_i\ge1,\ a_r\ge2\}.
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+Then, for every fixed \(s>2\),
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)\sim b(s)d^{-s}\qquad(d\to\infty),
+ \label{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}
+\end{equation}
+where the constant is the absolutely convergent one-large-partial-quotient
+context sum
+\begin{equation}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ b(s)
+ &: =\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal L}
+       \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal R}
+       \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\\
+ &=2\left(\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}\right)^2>0.
+ \end{aligned}
+ \label{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, this identifies the polynomial scale of every fixed
+low-temperature denominator layer; no tail hypothesis is used in
+\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\), with
+\(|\varnothing|_1=0\).  The canonical regular continued fraction of a reduced
+\(p/q\in(0,1)\) is
+\[
+ \frac pq=[0;a_1,\ldots,a_r],
+ \qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_r\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\).  The conversion formula
+used in the proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} gives
+\[
+ d(p/q)=|\mathbf a|_1-1.
+\]
+Consequently, on putting \(n=d+1\), the left side of
+\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer} is
+\begin{equation}
+ A_n(s):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf a\in\mathcal R\\|\mathbf a|_1=n}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-s}.
+ \label{eq:regular-continuant-layer}
+\end{equation}
+
+We first evaluate the context mass.  Canonical words in \(\mathcal R\) with
+denominator \(q\) parameterize the \(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in
+\((0,1)\).  Hence, for \(s>2\),
+\begin{equation}
+ R_s:=\sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal R}\mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s}
+ =1+\sum_{q\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(q)}{q^s}
+ =\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}<\infty.
+ \label{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}
+\end{equation}
+Every nonempty positive word either ends in a digit at least two or has the
+form \((a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)\).  The usual terminal move
+\[
+ (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)
+ \longleftrightarrow
+ (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1}+1)
+\]
+preserves the continuant.  It pairs the two regular expansions of every
+nonempty canonical word; it also pairs \((1)\) with \(\varnothing\).  Therefore
+\begin{equation}
+ L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal L}\mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+ =2R_s.
+ \label{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}
+\end{equation}
+This proves the absolute convergence and the evaluation in
+\eqref{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}.
+
+It remains to prove that this context sum is the whole local main term.  We
+give the cutoff argument, including the multiple-large-digit and moderate
+parts.  The continuant concatenation formula implies, for finite positive
+words \(\mathbf u,\mathbf v\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u\mathbf v)
+ \ge \mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v).
+ \label{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound}
+\end{equation}
+Moreover, with the two contexts fixed and \(a\to\infty\), multilinearity of
+the tridiagonal determinant defining the continuant gives
+\begin{equation}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)
+ =a\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)+O_{\mathbf u,\mathbf v}(1).
+ \label{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine}
+\end{equation}
+
+Let \(P_n(s)\) be the part of \eqref{eq:regular-continuant-layer} coming from
+words having a digit greater than \(n/2\).  Such a digit is unique.  Cutting
+there is a bijection with pairs
+\((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\in\mathcal L\times\mathcal R\) satisfying
+\(|\mathbf u|_1+|\mathbf v|_1<n/2\), the middle digit being
+\(a=n-|\mathbf u|_1-|\mathbf v|_1\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} and
+\eqref{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine} give, respectively,
+\[
+ n^s\mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)^{-s}
+ \le 2^s\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}
+\]
+and pointwise convergence of the left side to
+\(\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\).  Dominated
+convergence, using \eqref{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}--
+\eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, therefore yields
+\begin{equation}
+ n^sP_n(s)\longrightarrow L_sR_s=b(s).
+ \label{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}
+\end{equation}
+
+We now show that the complementary words have total weight \(o(n^{-s})\).
+Choose
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{s}{2(s-1)}<\delta<1,
+ \qquad h=\lfloor n^\delta\rfloor,
+ \label{eq:large-digit-cutoff}
+\end{equation}
+and set
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal L\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+By \eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).  A word having
+at least two digits not smaller than \(h\) can be cut at its first two such
+digits.  After dropping the restrictions on the three intervening contexts,
+\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} bounds its total weight by
+\begin{equation}
+ L_s^2R_s
+ \left(\sum_{a\ge h}a^{-s}\right)^2
+ =O_s(h^{2-2s})=o(n^{-s}),
+ \label{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}
+\end{equation}
+where the last equality is precisely the first inequality in
+\eqref{eq:large-digit-cutoff}.
+
+For completeness, consider a word all of whose digits are smaller than
+\(h\).  Greedily divide it into consecutive blocks: close a block as soon as
+its digit sum reaches \(h\), and leave the last remainder unclosed.  Every
+closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum at least
+\(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.  The
+concatenation bound and the uniqueness of the greedy decomposition show that
+the total continuant weight of all such words is at most
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1}
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+for all sufficiently large \(h\).  When \(N\ge n/4\), this is
+\(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A>0\), because \(n/h\to\infty\) and
+\(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+
+The words not counted by \(P_n(s)\) and not covered by
+\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible} have at most one digit at least \(h\).
+If there is none, apply \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} with \(N=n\).  If
+there is exactly one, its value is at most \(n/2\), so the two surrounding
+moderate contexts have combined digit sum at least \(n/2\); one has digit sum
+at least \(n/4\).  Cutting at the exceptional digit, summing its weight
+\(a^{-s}\), and applying \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} to that long context
+again gives \(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A\).  Together with
+\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}, this proves
+\[
+ A_n(s)-P_n(s)=o(n^{-s}).
+\]
+Combining this with \eqref{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}, and replacing
+\(n=d+1\) by \(d\), proves \eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic critical stable renewal]
+\label{thm:arithmetic-critical-stable-renewal}
+Put \(\alpha:=\sigma_0-1\in(1,2)\), and under the critical letter law put
+\[
+ \Pr\{(C,H)=(c(p/q),\log q)\}=q^{-\sigma_0}.
+\]
+Then \(\Pr\{C=2d+1\}=b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)\), and the explicit constants
+\begin{equation}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ b_C&:=
+ \sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal L}
+ \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal R}
+ \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-\sigma_0}
+ =2\left(\frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}\right)^2=8,\\
+ K_C&:=\frac{2^{\sigma_0-1}}{\sigma_0-1}b_C
+ =\frac{2^{\sigma_0+2}}{\sigma_0-1}
+ \end{aligned}
+ \label{eq:critical-tail-constants}
+\end{equation}
+are positive.  The double series defining \(b_C\) is absolutely convergent,
+and
+\begin{align}
+ b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)&\sim b_Cd^{-\sigma_0},
+ &&d\to\infty,
+ \label{eq:critical-letter-local-tail}\\
+ \Pr\{C>x\}
+ &=\sum_{q\ge2}q^{-\sigma_0}
+   \card{\{1\le p<q:(p,q)=1,\ c(p/q)>x\}}
+ \sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0},
+ &&x\to\infty.
+ \label{eq:critical-letter-tail}
+\end{align}
+If \(u_j=u_j(\sigma_0)\) is the renewal sequence in
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-coefficients}, then
+\begin{equation}
+ u_j=\frac1{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)}j^{2-\sigma_0}
+ +o(j^{2-\sigma_0}).
+ \label{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}
+\end{equation}
+Consequently,
+\begin{align}
+ Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)
+ &=\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
+   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order}\\
+ S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
+ &=\frac{4m}{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{4K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
+   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}).
+ \label{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}
+\end{align}
+Finally, \(C\) belongs to the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive
+\(\alpha\)-stable law.  More precisely, if \(a_n>0\) is chosen so that
+\(n\Pr\{C>a_n\}\to1\), then for independent copies \(C_1,C_2,\ldots\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{C_1+\cdots+C_n-n\mu_C}{a_n}
+ \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\mathcal S_\alpha,
+ \label{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}
+\end{equation}
+where \(\mathcal S_\alpha\) is the spectrally positive \(\alpha\)-stable law
+whose L\'evy measure has density \(\alpha x^{-\alpha-1}\) on \((0,\infty)\).
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The critical equation \eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} makes the displayed
+letter law a probability measure.  The local estimate
+\eqref{eq:critical-letter-local-tail} and the context-sum evaluation in
+\eqref{eq:critical-tail-constants} are \Cref{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
+at \(s=\sigma_0\).  Direct summation of that local estimate gives
+\[
+ \Pr\{C>x\}
+ =\sum_{d>(x-1)/2}b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)
+ \sim\frac{b_C}{\sigma_0-1}
+      \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^{1-\sigma_0},
+\]
+which is \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail} with the stated \(K_C\).  Thus
+regular variation is a conclusion of the arithmetic continuant estimate, not
+an assumption.
+
+The distribution of \(C\) has span one, finite mean \(\mu_C\), and tail
+\(K_Cj^{-\alpha}\), with \(1<\alpha<2\).  The second-order arithmetic renewal
+theorem for a finite-mean lattice law therefore gives
+\[
+ u_j-\frac1{\mu_C}
+ \sim\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\alpha-1)}j^{1-\alpha};
+\]
+see \cite[Ch.~XI]{Feller1971} for the arithmetic renewal theorem and its
+generating-function remainder argument.  Substitution of
+\(\alpha=\sigma_0-1\) proves
+\eqref{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}.  Summing it and using
+\[
+ \sum_{j=1}^{m-1}j^{2-\sigma_0}
+ \sim\frac{m^{3-\sigma_0}}{3-\sigma_0}
+\]
+in the exact identities \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-window-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order} and
+\eqref{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}; the boundary terms are
+\(O(1)=o(m^{3-\sigma_0})\).
+
+Finally, \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail}, finite mean, and the absence of a
+negative tail are precisely the one-sided domain-of-attraction conditions for
+an \(\alpha\)-stable law with the normalization in
+\eqref{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}; see \cite[Ch.~XVII]{Feller1971}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic denominator-layer theorem]
+\label{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
+For a finite word \(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\) of positive integers, let
+\(\mathcal K(\mathbf a)\) be its regular continuant, with
+\[
+ \begin{gathered}
+  \mathcal K(\varnothing)=1,\qquad \mathcal K(a_1)=a_1,\\
+  \mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)
+  =a_r\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1})
+   +\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-2}).
+ \end{gathered}
+\]
+Put
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+  \mathcal L&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
+   \bigcup_{r\ge1}\mathbb N^r,\\
+  \mathcal R&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
+   \{(a_1,\ldots,a_r):r\ge1,\ a_i\ge1,\ a_r\ge2\}.
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+Then, for every fixed \(s>2\),
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)\sim b(s)d^{-s}\qquad(d\to\infty),
+ \label{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}
+\end{equation}
+where the constant is the absolutely convergent one-large-partial-quotient
+context sum
+\begin{equation}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ b(s)
+ &: =\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal L}
+       \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal R}
+       \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\\
+ &=2\left(\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}\right)^2>0.
+ \end{aligned}
+ \label{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, this identifies the polynomial scale of every fixed
+low-temperature denominator layer; no tail hypothesis is used in
+\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\), with
+\(|\varnothing|_1=0\).  The canonical regular continued fraction of a reduced
+\(p/q\in(0,1)\) is
+\[
+ \frac pq=[0;a_1,\ldots,a_r],
+ \qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_r\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\).  The conversion formula
+used in the proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} gives
+\[
+ d(p/q)=|\mathbf a|_1-1.
+\]
+Consequently, on putting \(n=d+1\), the left side of
+\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer} is
+\begin{equation}
+ A_n(s):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf a\in\mathcal R\\|\mathbf a|_1=n}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-s}.
+ \label{eq:regular-continuant-layer}
+\end{equation}
+
+We first evaluate the context mass.  Canonical words in \(\mathcal R\) with
+denominator \(q\) parameterize the \(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in
+\((0,1)\).  Hence, for \(s>2\),
+\begin{equation}
+ R_s:=\sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal R}\mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s}
+ =1+\sum_{q\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(q)}{q^s}
+ =\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}<\infty.
+ \label{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}
+\end{equation}
+Every nonempty positive word either ends in a digit at least two or has the
+form \((a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)\).  The usual terminal move
+\[
+ (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)
+ \longleftrightarrow
+ (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1}+1)
+\]
+preserves the continuant.  It pairs the two regular expansions of every
+nonempty canonical word; it also pairs \((1)\) with \(\varnothing\).  Therefore
+\begin{equation}
+ L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal L}\mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+ =2R_s.
+ \label{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}
+\end{equation}
+This proves the absolute convergence and the evaluation in
+\eqref{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}.
+
+It remains to prove that this context sum is the whole local main term.  We
+give the cutoff argument, including the multiple-large-digit and moderate
+parts.  The continuant concatenation formula implies, for finite positive
+words \(\mathbf u,\mathbf v\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u\mathbf v)
+ \ge \mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v).
+ \label{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound}
+\end{equation}
+Moreover, with the two contexts fixed and \(a\to\infty\), multilinearity of
+the tridiagonal determinant defining the continuant gives
+\begin{equation}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)
+ =a\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)+O_{\mathbf u,\mathbf v}(1).
+ \label{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine}
+\end{equation}
+
+Let \(P_n(s)\) be the part of \eqref{eq:regular-continuant-layer} coming from
+words having a digit greater than \(n/2\).  Such a digit is unique.  Cutting
+there is a bijection with pairs
+\((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\in\mathcal L\times\mathcal R\) satisfying
+\(|\mathbf u|_1+|\mathbf v|_1<n/2\), the middle digit being
+\(a=n-|\mathbf u|_1-|\mathbf v|_1\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} and
+\eqref{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine} give, respectively,
+\[
+ n^s\mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)^{-s}
+ \le 2^s\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}
+\]
+and pointwise convergence of the left side to
+\(\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\).  Dominated
+convergence, using \eqref{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}--
+\eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, therefore yields
+\begin{equation}
+ n^sP_n(s)\longrightarrow L_sR_s=b(s).
+ \label{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}
+\end{equation}
+
+We now show that the complementary words have total weight \(o(n^{-s})\).
+Choose
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{s}{2(s-1)}<\delta<1,
+ \qquad h=\lfloor n^\delta\rfloor,
+ \label{eq:large-digit-cutoff}
+\end{equation}
+and set
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal L\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+By \eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).  A word having
+at least two digits not smaller than \(h\) can be cut at its first two such
+digits.  After dropping the restrictions on the three intervening contexts,
+\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} bounds its total weight by
+\begin{equation}
+ L_s^2R_s
+ \left(\sum_{a\ge h}a^{-s}\right)^2
+ =O_s(h^{2-2s})=o(n^{-s}),
+ \label{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}
+\end{equation}
+where the last equality is precisely the first inequality in
+\eqref{eq:large-digit-cutoff}.
+
+For completeness, consider a word all of whose digits are smaller than
+\(h\).  Greedily divide it into consecutive blocks: close a block as soon as
+its digit sum reaches \(h\), and leave the last remainder unclosed.  Every
+closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum at least
+\(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.  The
+concatenation bound and the uniqueness of the greedy decomposition show that
+the total continuant weight of all such words is at most
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1}
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+for all sufficiently large \(h\).  When \(N\ge n/4\), this is
+\(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A>0\), because \(n/h\to\infty\) and
+\(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+
+The words not counted by \(P_n(s)\) and not covered by
+\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible} have at most one digit at least \(h\).
+If there is none, apply \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} with \(N=n\).  If
+there is exactly one, its value is at most \(n/2\), so the two surrounding
+moderate contexts have combined digit sum at least \(n/2\); one has digit sum
+at least \(n/4\).  Cutting at the exceptional digit, summing its weight
+\(a^{-s}\), and applying \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} to that long context
+again gives \(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A\).  Together with
+\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}, this proves
+\[
+ A_n(s)-P_n(s)=o(n^{-s}).
+\]
+Combining this with \eqref{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}, and replacing
+\(n=d+1\) by \(d\), proves \eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic critical stable renewal]
+\label{thm:arithmetic-critical-stable-renewal}
+Put \(\alpha:=\sigma_0-1\in(1,2)\), and under the critical letter law put
+\[
+ \Pr\{(C,H)=(c(p/q),\log q)\}=q^{-\sigma_0}.
+\]
+Then \(\Pr\{C=2d+1\}=b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)\), and the explicit constants
+\begin{equation}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ b_C&:=
+ \sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal L}
+ \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal R}
+ \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-\sigma_0}
+ =2\left(\frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}\right)^2=8,\\
+ K_C&:=\frac{2^{\sigma_0-1}}{\sigma_0-1}b_C
+ =\frac{2^{\sigma_0+2}}{\sigma_0-1}
+ \end{aligned}
+ \label{eq:critical-tail-constants}
+\end{equation}
+are positive.  The double series defining \(b_C\) is absolutely convergent,
+and
+\begin{align}
+ b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)&\sim b_Cd^{-\sigma_0},
+ &&d\to\infty,
+ \label{eq:critical-letter-local-tail}\\
+ \Pr\{C>x\}
+ &=\sum_{q\ge2}q^{-\sigma_0}
+   \card{\{1\le p<q:(p,q)=1,\ c(p/q)>x\}}
+ \sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0},
+ &&x\to\infty.
+ \label{eq:critical-letter-tail}
+\end{align}
+If \(u_j=u_j(\sigma_0)\) is the renewal sequence in
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-coefficients}, then
+\begin{equation}
+ u_j=\frac1{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)}j^{2-\sigma_0}
+ +o(j^{2-\sigma_0}).
+ \label{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}
+\end{equation}
+Consequently,
+\begin{align}
+ Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)
+ &=\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
+   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order}\\
+ S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
+ &=\frac{4m}{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{4K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
+   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}).
+ \label{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}
+\end{align}
+Finally, \(C\) belongs to the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive
+\(\alpha\)-stable law.  More precisely, if \(a_n>0\) is chosen so that
+\(n\Pr\{C>a_n\}\to1\), then for independent copies \(C_1,C_2,\ldots\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{C_1+\cdots+C_n-n\mu_C}{a_n}
+ \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\mathcal S_\alpha,
+ \label{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}
+\end{equation}
+where \(\mathcal S_\alpha\) is the spectrally positive \(\alpha\)-stable law
+whose L\'evy measure has density \(\alpha x^{-\alpha-1}\) on \((0,\infty)\).
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The critical equation \eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} makes the displayed
+letter law a probability measure.  The local estimate
+\eqref{eq:critical-letter-local-tail} and the context-sum evaluation in
+\eqref{eq:critical-tail-constants} are \Cref{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
+at \(s=\sigma_0\).  Direct summation of that local estimate gives
+\[
+ \Pr\{C>x\}
+ =\sum_{d>(x-1)/2}b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)
+ \sim\frac{b_C}{\sigma_0-1}
+      \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^{1-\sigma_0},
+\]
+which is \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail} with the stated \(K_C\).  Thus
+regular variation is a conclusion of the arithmetic continuant estimate, not
+an assumption.
+
+The distribution of \(C\) has span one, finite mean \(\mu_C\), and tail
+\(K_Cj^{-\alpha}\), with \(1<\alpha<2\).  The second-order arithmetic renewal
+theorem for a finite-mean lattice law therefore gives
+\[
+ u_j-\frac1{\mu_C}
+ \sim\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\alpha-1)}j^{1-\alpha};
+\]
+see \cite[Ch.~XI]{Feller1971} for the arithmetic renewal theorem and its
+generating-function remainder argument.  Substitution of
+\(\alpha=\sigma_0-1\) proves
+\eqref{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}.  Summing it and using
+\[
+ \sum_{j=1}^{m-1}j^{2-\sigma_0}
+ \sim\frac{m^{3-\sigma_0}}{3-\sigma_0}
+\]
+in the exact identities \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-window-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order} and
+\eqref{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}; the boundary terms are
+\(O(1)=o(m^{3-\sigma_0})\).
+
+Finally, \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail}, finite mean, and the absence of a
+negative tail are precisely the one-sided domain-of-attraction conditions for
+an \(\alpha\)-stable law with the normalization in
+\eqref{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}; see \cite[Ch.~XVII]{Feller1971}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic denominator-layer theorem]
+\label{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
+For a finite word \(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\) of positive integers, let
+\(\mathcal K(\mathbf a)\) be its regular continuant, with
+\[
+ \begin{gathered}
+  \mathcal K(\varnothing)=1,\qquad \mathcal K(a_1)=a_1,\\
+  \mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)
+  =a_r\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1})
+   +\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-2}).
+ \end{gathered}
+\]
+Put
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+  \mathcal C_{\rm L}&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
+   \bigcup_{r\ge1}\mathbb N^r,\\
+  \mathcal C_{\rm R}&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
+   \{(a_1,\ldots,a_r):r\ge1,\ a_i\ge1,\ a_r\ge2\}.
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+Then, for every fixed \(s>2\),
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)\sim b(s)d^{-s}\qquad(d\to\infty),
+ \label{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}
+\end{equation}
+where the constant is the absolutely convergent one-large-partial-quotient
+context sum
+\begin{equation}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ b(s)
+ &: =\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+       \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}
+       \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\\
+ &=2\left(\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}\right)^2>0.
+ \end{aligned}
+ \label{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, this identifies the polynomial scale of every fixed
+low-temperature denominator layer; no tail hypothesis is used in
+\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\), with
+\(|\varnothing|_1=0\).  The canonical regular continued fraction of a reduced
+\(p/q\in(0,1)\) is
+\[
+ \frac pq=[0;a_1,\ldots,a_r],
+ \qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_r\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\).  The conversion formula
+used in the proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} gives
+\[
+ d(p/q)=|\mathbf a|_1-1.
+\]
+Consequently, on putting \(n=d+1\), the left side of
+\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer} is
+\begin{equation}
+ A_n(s):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf a\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\|\mathbf a|_1=n}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-s}.
+ \label{eq:regular-continuant-layer}
+\end{equation}
+
+We first evaluate the context mass.  Canonical words in
+\(\mathcal C_{\rm R}\) with
+denominator \(q\) parameterize the \(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in
+\((0,1)\).  Hence, for \(s>2\),
+\begin{equation}
+ R_s:=\sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}\mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s}
+ =1+\sum_{q\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(q)}{q^s}
+ =\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}<\infty.
+ \label{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}
+\end{equation}
+Every nonempty positive word either ends in a digit at least two or has the
+form \((a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)\).  The usual terminal move
+\[
+ (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)
+ \longleftrightarrow
+ (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1}+1)
+\]
+preserves the continuant.  It pairs the two regular expansions of every
+nonempty canonical word; it also pairs \((1)\) with \(\varnothing\).  Therefore
+\begin{equation}
+ L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}\mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+ =2R_s.
+ \label{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}
+\end{equation}
+This proves the absolute convergence and the evaluation in
+\eqref{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}.
+
+It remains to prove that this context sum is the whole local main term.  We
+give the cutoff argument, including the multiple-large-digit and moderate
+parts.  The continuant concatenation formula implies, for finite positive
+words \(\mathbf u,\mathbf v\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u\mathbf v)
+ \ge \mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v).
+ \label{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound}
+\end{equation}
+Moreover, with the two contexts fixed and \(a\to\infty\), multilinearity of
+the tridiagonal determinant defining the continuant gives
+\begin{equation}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)
+ =a\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)+O_{\mathbf u,\mathbf v}(1).
+ \label{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine}
+\end{equation}
+
+Let \(P_n(s)\) be the part of \eqref{eq:regular-continuant-layer} coming from
+words having a digit greater than \(n/2\).  Such a digit is unique.  Cutting
+there is a bijection with pairs
+\((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\times\mathcal C_{\rm R}\)
+satisfying
+\(|\mathbf u|_1+|\mathbf v|_1<n/2\), the middle digit being
+\(a=n-|\mathbf u|_1-|\mathbf v|_1\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} and
+\eqref{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine} give, respectively,
+\[
+ n^s\mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)^{-s}
+ \le 2^s\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}
+\]
+and pointwise convergence of the left side to
+\(\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\).  Dominated
+convergence, using \eqref{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}--
+\eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, therefore yields
+\begin{equation}
+ n^sP_n(s)\longrightarrow L_sR_s=b(s).
+ \label{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}
+\end{equation}
+
+We now show that the complementary words have total weight \(o(n^{-s})\).
+Choose
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{s}{2(s-1)}<\delta<1,
+ \qquad h=\lfloor n^\delta\rfloor,
+ \label{eq:large-digit-cutoff}
+\end{equation}
+and set
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+By \eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).  A word having
+at least two digits not smaller than \(h\) can be cut at its first two such
+digits.  After dropping the restrictions on the three intervening contexts,
+\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} bounds its total weight by
+\begin{equation}
+ L_s^2R_s
+ \left(\sum_{a\ge h}a^{-s}\right)^2
+ =O_s(h^{2-2s})=o(n^{-s}),
+ \label{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}
+\end{equation}
+where the last equality is precisely the first inequality in
+\eqref{eq:large-digit-cutoff}.
+
+For completeness, consider a word all of whose digits are smaller than
+\(h\).  Greedily divide it into consecutive blocks: close a block as soon as
+its digit sum reaches \(h\), and leave the last remainder unclosed.  Every
+closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum at least
+\(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.  The
+concatenation bound and the uniqueness of the greedy decomposition show that
+the total continuant weight of all such words is at most
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1}
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+for all sufficiently large \(h\).  When \(N\ge n/4\), this is
+\(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A>0\), because \(n/h\to\infty\) and
+\(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+
+The words not counted by \(P_n(s)\) and not covered by
+\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible} have at most one digit at least \(h\).
+If there is none, apply \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} with \(N=n\).  If
+there is exactly one, its value is at most \(n/2\), so the two surrounding
+moderate contexts have combined digit sum at least \(n/2\); one has digit sum
+at least \(n/4\).  Cutting at the exceptional digit, summing its weight
+\(a^{-s}\), and applying \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} to that long context
+again gives \(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A\).  Together with
+\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}, this proves
+\[
+ A_n(s)-P_n(s)=o(n^{-s}).
+\]
+Combining this with \eqref{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}, and replacing
+\(n=d+1\) by \(d\), proves \eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic critical stable renewal]
+\label{thm:arithmetic-critical-stable-renewal}
+Put \(\alpha:=\sigma_0-1\in(1,2)\), and under the critical letter law put
+\[
+ \Pr\{(C,H)=(c(p/q),\log q)\}=q^{-\sigma_0}.
+\]
+Then \(\Pr\{C=2d+1\}=b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)\), and the explicit constants
+\begin{equation}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ b_C&:=
+ \sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}
+ \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-\sigma_0}
+ =2\left(\frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}\right)^2=8,\\
+ K_C&:=\frac{2^{\sigma_0-1}}{\sigma_0-1}b_C
+ =\frac{2^{\sigma_0+2}}{\sigma_0-1}
+ \end{aligned}
+ \label{eq:critical-tail-constants}
+\end{equation}
+are positive.  The double series defining \(b_C\) is absolutely convergent,
+and
+\begin{align}
+ b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)&\sim b_Cd^{-\sigma_0},
+ &&d\to\infty,
+ \label{eq:critical-letter-local-tail}\\
+ \Pr\{C>x\}
+ &=\sum_{q\ge2}q^{-\sigma_0}
+   \card{\{1\le p<q:(p,q)=1,\ c(p/q)>x\}}
+ \sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0},
+ &&x\to\infty.
+ \label{eq:critical-letter-tail}
+\end{align}
+If \(u_j=u_j(\sigma_0)\) is the renewal sequence in
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-coefficients}, then
+\begin{equation}
+ u_j=\frac1{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)}j^{2-\sigma_0}
+ +o(j^{2-\sigma_0}).
+ \label{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}
+\end{equation}
+Consequently,
+\begin{align}
+ Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)
+ &=\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
+   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order}\\
+ S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
+ &=\frac{4m}{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{4K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
+   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}).
+ \label{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}
+\end{align}
+Finally, \(C\) belongs to the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive
+\(\alpha\)-stable law.  More precisely, if \(a_n>0\) is chosen so that
+\(n\Pr\{C>a_n\}\to1\), then for independent copies \(C_1,C_2,\ldots\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{C_1+\cdots+C_n-n\mu_C}{a_n}
+ \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\mathcal S_\alpha,
+ \label{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}
+\end{equation}
+where \(\mathcal S_\alpha\) is the spectrally positive \(\alpha\)-stable law
+whose L\'evy measure has density \(\alpha x^{-\alpha-1}\) on \((0,\infty)\).
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The critical equation \eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} makes the displayed
+letter law a probability measure.  The local estimate
+\eqref{eq:critical-letter-local-tail} and the context-sum evaluation in
+\eqref{eq:critical-tail-constants} are \Cref{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
+at \(s=\sigma_0\).  Direct summation of that local estimate gives
+\[
+ \Pr\{C>x\}
+ =\sum_{d>(x-1)/2}b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)
+ \sim\frac{b_C}{\sigma_0-1}
+      \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^{1-\sigma_0},
+\]
+which is \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail} with the stated \(K_C\).  Thus
+regular variation is a conclusion of the arithmetic continuant estimate, not
+an assumption.
+
+The distribution of \(C\) has span one, finite mean \(\mu_C\), and tail
+\(K_Cj^{-\alpha}\), with \(1<\alpha<2\).  The second-order arithmetic renewal
+theorem for a finite-mean lattice law therefore gives
+\[
+ u_j-\frac1{\mu_C}
+ \sim\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\alpha-1)}j^{1-\alpha};
+\]
+see \cite[Ch.~XI]{Feller1971} for the arithmetic renewal theorem and its
+generating-function remainder argument.  Substitution of
+\(\alpha=\sigma_0-1\) proves
+\eqref{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}.  Summing it and using
+\[
+ \sum_{j=1}^{m-1}j^{2-\sigma_0}
+ \sim\frac{m^{3-\sigma_0}}{3-\sigma_0}
+\]
+in the exact identities \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-window-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order} and
+\eqref{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}; the boundary terms are
+\(O(1)=o(m^{3-\sigma_0})\).
+
+Finally, \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail}, finite mean, and the absence of a
+negative tail are precisely the one-sided domain-of-attraction conditions for
+an \(\alpha\)-stable law with the normalization in
+\eqref{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}; see \cite[Ch.~XVII]{Feller1971}.
+\end{proof}

-\begin{remark}[Open second-order critical-cost interface]
-\label{rem:critical-cost-tail-open-interface}
-The preceding theorem uses only exponential rates and does not identify a
-second-order critical renewal term.  Such a result would require, at a
-minimum, a uniform mixed-denominator estimate of the form
-\[
- \sum_{q\ge2}q^{-\sigma_0}
- \card{\{1\le p<q:(p,q)=1,\ c(p/q)>x\}}
- \sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0}\qquad(x\to\infty)
-\]
-with \(K_C>0\), including a proof that multiple large partial quotients and
-possible lattice oscillations are lower order.  Fixed-denominator estimates
-such as \cite{AistleitnerBordaHauke2023} do not by themselves provide the
-uniform summation in the critical range \(q\asymp x\).  No such regular
-variation statement, and hence no \(m^{3-\sigma_0}\) correction to the
-critical partition sum, is asserted here.
-\end{remark}

+\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic denominator-layer theorem]
+\label{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
+For a finite word \(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\) of positive integers, let
+\(\mathcal K(\mathbf a)\) be its regular continuant, with
+\[
+ \begin{gathered}
+  \mathcal K(\varnothing)=1,\qquad \mathcal K(a_1)=a_1,\\
+  \mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)
+  =a_r\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1})
+   +\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-2}).
+ \end{gathered}
+\]
+Put
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+  \mathcal C_{\rm L}&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
+   \bigcup_{r\ge1}\mathbb N^r,\\
+  \mathcal C_{\rm R}&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
+   \{(a_1,\ldots,a_r):r\ge1,\ a_i\ge1,\ a_r\ge2\}.
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+Then, for every fixed \(s>2\),
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)\sim b(s)d^{-s}\qquad(d\to\infty),
+ \label{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}
+\end{equation}
+where the constant is the absolutely convergent one-large-partial-quotient
+context sum
+\begin{equation}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ b(s)
+ &: =\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+       \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}
+       \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\\
+ &=2\left(\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}\right)^2>0.
+ \end{aligned}
+ \label{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, this identifies the polynomial scale of every fixed
+low-temperature denominator layer; no tail hypothesis is used in
+\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\), with
+\(|\varnothing|_1=0\).  The canonical regular continued fraction of a reduced
+\(p/q\in(0,1)\) is
+\[
+ \frac pq=[0;a_1,\ldots,a_r],
+ \qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_r\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\).  The conversion formula
+used in the proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} gives
+\[
+ d(p/q)=|\mathbf a|_1-1.
+\]
+Consequently, on putting \(n=d+1\), the left side of
+\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer} is
+\begin{equation}
+ A_n(s):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf a\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\|\mathbf a|_1=n}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-s}.
+ \label{eq:regular-continuant-layer}
+\end{equation}
+
+We first evaluate the context mass.  Canonical words in
+\(\mathcal C_{\rm R}\) with
+denominator \(q\) parameterize the \(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in
+\((0,1)\).  Hence, for \(s>2\),
+\begin{equation}
+ R_s:=\sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}\mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s}
+ =1+\sum_{q\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(q)}{q^s}
+ =\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}<\infty.
+ \label{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}
+\end{equation}
+Every nonempty positive word either ends in a digit at least two or has the
+form \((a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)\).  The usual terminal move
+\[
+ (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)
+ \longleftrightarrow
+ (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1}+1)
+\]
+preserves the continuant.  It pairs the two regular expansions of every
+nonempty canonical word; it also pairs \((1)\) with \(\varnothing\).  Therefore
+\begin{equation}
+ L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}\mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+ =2R_s.
+ \label{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}
+\end{equation}
+This proves the absolute convergence and the evaluation in
+\eqref{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}.
+
+It remains to prove that this context sum is the whole local main term.  We
+give the cutoff argument, including the multiple-large-digit and moderate
+parts.  The continuant concatenation formula implies, for finite positive
+words \(\mathbf u,\mathbf v\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u\mathbf v)
+ \ge \mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v).
+ \label{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound}
+\end{equation}
+Moreover, with the two contexts fixed and \(a\to\infty\), multilinearity of
+the tridiagonal determinant defining the continuant gives
+\begin{equation}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)
+ =a\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)+O_{\mathbf u,\mathbf v}(1).
+ \label{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine}
+\end{equation}
+
+Let \(P_n(s)\) be the part of \eqref{eq:regular-continuant-layer} coming from
+words having a digit greater than \(n/2\).  Such a digit is unique.  Cutting
+there is a bijection with pairs
+\((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\times\mathcal C_{\rm R}\)
+satisfying
+\(|\mathbf u|_1+|\mathbf v|_1<n/2\), the middle digit being
+\(a=n-|\mathbf u|_1-|\mathbf v|_1\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} and
+\eqref{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine} give, respectively,
+\[
+ n^s\mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)^{-s}
+ \le 2^s\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}
+\]
+and pointwise convergence of the left side to
+\(\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\).  Dominated
+convergence, using \eqref{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}--
+\eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, therefore yields
+\begin{equation}
+ n^sP_n(s)\longrightarrow L_sR_s=b(s).
+ \label{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}
+\end{equation}
+

+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{s}{2(s-1)}<\delta<1,
+ \qquad h=\lfloor n^\delta\rfloor,
+ \label{eq:large-digit-cutoff}
+\end{equation}
+and set
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}

+at least two digits not smaller than \(h\) can be cut at its first two such

+\begin{equation}
+ L_s^2R_s
+ \left(\sum_{a\ge h}a^{-s}\right)^2
+ =O_s(h^{2-2s})=o(n^{-s}),
+ \label{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}
+\end{equation}
+where the last equality is precisely the first inequality in
+\eqref{eq:large-digit-cutoff}.
+
+For completeness, consider a word all of whose digits are smaller than
+\(h\).  Greedily divide it into consecutive blocks: close a block as soon as
+its digit sum reaches \(h\), and leave the last remainder unclosed.  Every
+closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum at least
+\(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.  The
+concatenation bound and the uniqueness of the greedy decomposition show that
+the total continuant weight of all such words is at most
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1}
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+for all sufficiently large \(h\).  When \(N\ge n/4\), this is
+\(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A>0\), because \(n/h\to\infty\) and
+\(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+
+The words not counted by \(P_n(s)\) and not covered by
+\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible} have at most one digit at least \(h\).
+If there is none, apply \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} with \(N=n\).  If
+there is exactly one, its value is at most \(n/2\), so the two surrounding
+moderate contexts have combined digit sum at least \(n/2\); one has digit sum
+at least \(n/4\).  Cutting at the exceptional digit, summing its weight
+\(a^{-s}\), and applying \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} to that long context
+again gives \(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A\).  Together with
+\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}, this proves
+\[
+ A_n(s)-P_n(s)=o(n^{-s}).
+\]
+Combining this with \eqref{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}, and replacing
+\(n=d+1\) by \(d\), proves \eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic critical stable renewal]
+\label{thm:arithmetic-critical-stable-renewal}
+Put \(\alpha:=\sigma_0-1\in(1,2)\), and under the critical letter law put
+\[
+ \Pr\{(C,H)=(c(p/q),\log q)\}=q^{-\sigma_0}.
+\]
+Then \(\Pr\{C=2d+1\}=b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)\), and the explicit constants
+\begin{equation}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ b_C&:=
+ \sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}
+ \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-\sigma_0}
+ =2\left(\frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}\right)^2=8,\\
+ K_C&:=\frac{2^{\sigma_0-1}}{\sigma_0-1}b_C
+ =\frac{2^{\sigma_0+2}}{\sigma_0-1}
+ \end{aligned}
+ \label{eq:critical-tail-constants}
+\end{equation}
+are positive.  The double series defining \(b_C\) is absolutely convergent,
+and
+\begin{align}
+ b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)&\sim b_Cd^{-\sigma_0},
+ &&d\to\infty,
+ \label{eq:critical-letter-local-tail}\\
+ \Pr\{C>x\}
+ &=\sum_{q\ge2}q^{-\sigma_0}
+   \card{\{1\le p<q:(p,q)=1,\ c(p/q)>x\}}
+ \sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0},
+ &&x\to\infty.
+ \label{eq:critical-letter-tail}
+\end{align}
+If \(u_j=u_j(\sigma_0)\) is the renewal sequence in
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-coefficients}, then
+\begin{equation}
+ u_j=\frac1{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)}j^{2-\sigma_0}
+ +o(j^{2-\sigma_0}).
+ \label{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}
+\end{equation}
+Consequently,
+\begin{align}
+ Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)
+ &=\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
+   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order}\\
+ S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
+ &=\frac{4m}{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{4K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
+   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}).
+ \label{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}
+\end{align}
+Finally, \(C\) belongs to the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive
+\(\alpha\)-stable law.  More precisely, if \(a_n>0\) is chosen so that
+\(n\Pr\{C>a_n\}\to1\), then for independent copies \(C_1,C_2,\ldots\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{C_1+\cdots+C_n-n\mu_C}{a_n}
+ \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\mathcal S_\alpha,
+ \label{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}
+\end{equation}
+where \(\mathcal S_\alpha\) is the spectrally positive \(\alpha\)-stable law
+whose L\'evy measure has density \(\alpha x^{-\alpha-1}\) on \((0,\infty)\).
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The critical equation \eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} makes the displayed
+letter law a probability measure.  The local estimate
+\eqref{eq:critical-letter-local-tail} and the context-sum evaluation in
+\eqref{eq:critical-tail-constants} are \Cref{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
+at \(s=\sigma_0\).  Direct summation of that local estimate gives
+\[
+ \Pr\{C>x\}
+ =\sum_{d>(x-1)/2}b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)
+ \sim\frac{b_C}{\sigma_0-1}
+      \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^{1-\sigma_0},
+\]
+which is \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail} with the stated \(K_C\).  Thus
+regular variation is a conclusion of the arithmetic continuant estimate, not
+an assumption.
+
+The distribution of \(C\) has span one, finite mean \(\mu_C\), and tail
+\(K_Cj^{-\alpha}\), with \(1<\alpha<2\).  The second-order arithmetic renewal
+theorem for a finite-mean lattice law therefore gives
+\[
+ u_j-\frac1{\mu_C}
+ \sim\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\alpha-1)}j^{1-\alpha};
+\]
+see \cite[Ch.~XI]{Feller1971} for the arithmetic renewal theorem and its
+generating-function remainder argument.  Substitution of
+\(\alpha=\sigma_0-1\) proves
+\eqref{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}.  Summing it and using
+\[
+ \sum_{j=1}^{m-1}j^{2-\sigma_0}
+ \sim\frac{m^{3-\sigma_0}}{3-\sigma_0}
+\]
+in the exact identities \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-window-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order} and
+\eqref{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}; the boundary terms are
+\(O(1)=o(m^{3-\sigma_0})\).
+
+Finally, \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail}, finite mean, and the absence of a
+negative tail are precisely the one-sided domain-of-attraction conditions for
+an \(\alpha\)-stable law with the normalization in
+\eqref{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}; see \cite[Ch.~XVII]{Feller1971}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic denominator-layer theorem]
+\label{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
+For a finite word \(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\) of positive integers, let
+\(\mathcal K(\mathbf a)\) be its regular continuant, with
+\[
+ \begin{gathered}
+  \mathcal K(\varnothing)=1,\qquad \mathcal K(a_1)=a_1,\\
+  \mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)
+  =a_r\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1})
+   +\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-2}).
+ \end{gathered}
+\]
+Put
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+  \mathcal C_{\rm L}&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
+   \bigcup_{r\ge1}\mathbb N^r,\\
+  \mathcal C_{\rm R}&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
+   \{(a_1,\ldots,a_r):r\ge1,\ a_i\ge1,\ a_r\ge2\}.
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+Then, for every fixed \(s>2\),
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)\sim b(s)d^{-s}\qquad(d\to\infty),
+ \label{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}
+\end{equation}
+where the constant is the absolutely convergent one-large-partial-quotient
+context sum
+\begin{equation}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ b(s)
+ &: =\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+       \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}
+       \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\\
+ &=2\left(\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}\right)^2>0.
+ \end{aligned}
+ \label{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, this identifies the polynomial scale of every fixed
+low-temperature denominator layer; no tail hypothesis is used in
+\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\), with
+\(|\varnothing|_1=0\).  The canonical regular continued fraction of a reduced
+\(p/q\in(0,1)\) is
+\[
+ \frac pq=[0;a_1,\ldots,a_r],
+ \qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_r\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\).  The conversion formula
+used in the proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} gives
+\[
+ d(p/q)=|\mathbf a|_1-1.
+\]
+Consequently, on putting \(n=d+1\), the left side of
+\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer} is
+\begin{equation}
+ A_n(s):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf a\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\|\mathbf a|_1=n}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-s}.
+ \label{eq:regular-continuant-layer}
+\end{equation}
+
+We first evaluate the context mass.  Canonical words in
+\(\mathcal C_{\rm R}\) with
+denominator \(q\) parameterize the \(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in
+\((0,1)\).  Hence, for \(s>2\),
+\begin{equation}
+ R_s:=\sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}\mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s}
+ =1+\sum_{q\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(q)}{q^s}
+ =\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}<\infty.
+ \label{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}
+\end{equation}
+Every nonempty positive word either ends in a digit at least two or has the
+form \((a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)\).  The usual terminal move
+\[
+ (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)
+ \longleftrightarrow
+ (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1}+1)
+\]
+preserves the continuant.  It pairs the two regular expansions of every
+nonempty canonical word; it also pairs \((1)\) with \(\varnothing\).  Therefore
+\begin{equation}
+ L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}\mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+ =2R_s.
+ \label{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}
+\end{equation}
+This proves the absolute convergence and the evaluation in
+\eqref{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}.
+
+It remains to prove that this context sum is the whole local main term.  We
+give the cutoff argument, including the multiple-large-digit and moderate
+parts.  The continuant concatenation formula implies, for finite positive
+words \(\mathbf u,\mathbf v\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u\mathbf v)
+ \ge \mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v).
+ \label{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound}
+\end{equation}
+Moreover, with the two contexts fixed and \(a\to\infty\), multilinearity of
+the tridiagonal determinant defining the continuant gives
+\begin{equation}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)
+ =a\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)+O_{\mathbf u,\mathbf v}(1).
+ \label{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine}
+\end{equation}
+
+Let \(P_n(s)\) be the part of \eqref{eq:regular-continuant-layer} coming from
+words having a digit greater than \(n/2\).  Such a digit is unique.  Cutting
+there is a bijection with pairs
+\((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\times\mathcal C_{\rm R}\)
+satisfying
+\(|\mathbf u|_1+|\mathbf v|_1<n/2\), the middle digit being
+\(a=n-|\mathbf u|_1-|\mathbf v|_1\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} and
+\eqref{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine} give, respectively,
+\[
+ n^s\mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)^{-s}
+ \le 2^s\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}
+\]
+and pointwise convergence of the left side to
+\(\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\).  Dominated
+convergence, using \eqref{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}--
+\eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, therefore yields
+\begin{equation}
+ n^sP_n(s)\longrightarrow L_sR_s=b(s).
+ \label{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}
+\end{equation}
+
+We now show that the complementary words have total weight \(o(n^{-s})\).
+Choose
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{s}{2(s-1)}<\delta<1,
+ \qquad h=\lfloor n^\delta\rfloor,
+ \label{eq:large-digit-cutoff}
+\end{equation}
+and set
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+By \eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).  A word having
+at least two digits not smaller than \(h\) can be cut at its first two such
+digits.  After dropping the restrictions on the three intervening contexts,
+\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} bounds its total weight by
+\begin{equation}
+ L_s^2R_s
+ \left(\sum_{a\ge h}a^{-s}\right)^2
+ =O_s(h^{2-2s})=o(n^{-s}),
+ \label{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}
+\end{equation}
+where the last equality is precisely the first inequality in
+\eqref{eq:large-digit-cutoff}.
+
+For completeness, consider a word all of whose digits are smaller than
+\(h\).  Greedily divide it into consecutive blocks: close a block as soon as
+its digit sum reaches \(h\), and leave the last remainder unclosed.  Every
+closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum at least
+\(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.  The
+concatenation bound and the uniqueness of the greedy decomposition show that
+the total continuant weight of all such words is at most
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1}
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+for all sufficiently large \(h\).  When \(N\ge n/4\), this is
+\(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A>0\), because \(n/h\to\infty\) and
+\(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+
+The words not counted by \(P_n(s)\) and not covered by
+\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible} have at most one digit at least \(h\).
+If there is none, apply \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} with \(N=n\).  If
+there is exactly one, its value is at most \(n/2\), so the two surrounding
+moderate contexts have combined digit sum at least \(n/2\); one has digit sum
+at least \(n/4\).  Cutting at the exceptional digit, summing its weight
+\(a^{-s}\), and applying \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} to that long context
+again gives \(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A\).  Together with
+\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}, this proves
+\[
+ A_n(s)-P_n(s)=o(n^{-s}).
+\]
+Combining this with \eqref{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}, and replacing
+\(n=d+1\) by \(d\), proves \eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic critical stable renewal]
+\label{thm:arithmetic-critical-stable-renewal}
+Put \(\alpha:=\sigma_0-1\in(1,2)\), and under the critical letter law put
+\[
+ \Pr\{(C,H)=(c(p/q),\log q)\}=q^{-\sigma_0}.
+\]
+Then \(\Pr\{C=2d+1\}=b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)\), and the explicit constants
+\begin{equation}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ b_C&:=
+ \sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}
+ \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-\sigma_0}
+ =2\left(\frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}\right)^2=8,\\
+ K_C&:=\frac{2^{\sigma_0-1}}{\sigma_0-1}b_C
+ =\frac{2^{\sigma_0+2}}{\sigma_0-1}
+ \end{aligned}
+ \label{eq:critical-tail-constants}
+\end{equation}
+are positive.  The double series defining \(b_C\) is absolutely convergent,
+and
+\begin{align}
+ b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)&\sim b_Cd^{-\sigma_0},
+ &&d\to\infty,
+ \label{eq:critical-letter-local-tail}\\
+ \Pr\{C>x\}
+ &=\sum_{q\ge2}q^{-\sigma_0}
+   \card{\{1\le p<q:(p,q)=1,\ c(p/q)>x\}},\notag\\
+ &\sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0},
+ &&x\to\infty.
+ \label{eq:critical-letter-tail}
+\end{align}
+If \(u_j=u_j(\sigma_0)\) is the renewal sequence in
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-coefficients}, then
+\begin{equation}
+ u_j=\frac1{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)}j^{2-\sigma_0}
+ +o(j^{2-\sigma_0}).
+ \label{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}
+\end{equation}
+Consequently,
+\begin{align}
+ Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)
+ &=\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
+   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order}\\
+ S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
+ &=\frac{4m}{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{4K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
+   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}).
+ \label{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}
+\end{align}
+Finally, \(C\) belongs to the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive
+\(\alpha\)-stable law.  More precisely, if \(a_n>0\) is chosen so that
+\(n\Pr\{C>a_n\}\to1\), then for independent copies \(C_1,C_2,\ldots\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{C_1+\cdots+C_n-n\mu_C}{a_n}
+ \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\mathcal S_\alpha,
+ \label{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}
+\end{equation}
+where \(\mathcal S_\alpha\) is the spectrally positive \(\alpha\)-stable law
+whose L\'evy measure has density \(\alpha x^{-\alpha-1}\) on \((0,\infty)\).
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The critical equation \eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} makes the displayed
+letter law a probability measure.  The local estimate
+\eqref{eq:critical-letter-local-tail} and the context-sum evaluation in
+\eqref{eq:critical-tail-constants} are \Cref{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
+at \(s=\sigma_0\).  Direct summation of that local estimate gives
+\[
+ \Pr\{C>x\}
+ =\sum_{d>(x-1)/2}b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)
+ \sim\frac{b_C}{\sigma_0-1}
+      \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^{1-\sigma_0},
+\]
+which is \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail} with the stated \(K_C\).  Thus
+regular variation is a conclusion of the arithmetic continuant estimate, not
+an assumption.
+
+The distribution of \(C\) has span one, finite mean \(\mu_C\), and tail
+\(K_Cj^{-\alpha}\), with \(1<\alpha<2\).  The finite-mean case of the
+discrete renewal-sequence theorem \cite{OmeyVanGulck2015} therefore gives
+\[
+ u_j-\frac1{\mu_C}
+ \sim\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\alpha-1)}j^{1-\alpha};
+\]
+the same coefficient also follows from the generating-function remainder
+argument for the arithmetic renewal theorem in \cite[Ch.~XI]{Feller1971}.
+Substitution of
+\(\alpha=\sigma_0-1\) proves
+\eqref{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}.  Summing it and using
+\[
+ \sum_{j=1}^{m-1}j^{2-\sigma_0}
+ \sim\frac{m^{3-\sigma_0}}{3-\sigma_0}
+\]
+in the exact identities \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-window-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order} and
+\eqref{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}; the boundary terms are
+\(O(1)=o(m^{3-\sigma_0})\).
+
+Finally, \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail}, finite mean, and the absence of a
+negative tail are precisely the one-sided domain-of-attraction conditions for
+an \(\alpha\)-stable law with the normalization in
+\eqref{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}; see \cite[Ch.~XVII]{Feller1971}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic denominator-layer theorem]
+\label{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
+For a finite word \(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\) of positive integers, let
+\(\mathcal K(\mathbf a)\) be its regular continuant, with
+\[
+ \begin{gathered}
+  \mathcal K(\varnothing)=1,\qquad \mathcal K(a_1)=a_1,\\
+  \mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)
+  =a_r\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1})
+   +\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-2}).
+ \end{gathered}
+\]
+Put
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+  \mathcal C_{\rm L}&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
+   \bigcup_{r\ge1}\mathbb N^r,\\
+  \mathcal C_{\rm R}&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
+   \{(a_1,\ldots,a_r):r\ge1,\ a_i\ge1,\ a_r\ge2\}.
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+Then, for every fixed \(s>2\),
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)\sim b(s)d^{-s}\qquad(d\to\infty),
+ \label{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}
+\end{equation}
+where the constant is the absolutely convergent one-large-partial-quotient
+context sum
+\begin{equation}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ b(s)
+ &: =\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+       \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}
+       \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\\
+ &=2\left(\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}\right)^2>0.
+ \end{aligned}
+ \label{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, this identifies the polynomial scale of every fixed
+low-temperature denominator layer; no tail hypothesis is used in
+\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\), with
+\(|\varnothing|_1=0\).  The canonical regular continued fraction of a reduced
+\(p/q\in(0,1)\) is
+\[
+ \frac pq=[0;a_1,\ldots,a_r],
+ \qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_r\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\).  The conversion formula
+used in the proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} gives
+\[
+ d(p/q)=|\mathbf a|_1-1.
+\]
+Consequently, on putting \(n=d+1\), the left side of
+\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer} is
+\begin{equation}
+ A_n(s):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf a\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\|\mathbf a|_1=n}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-s}.
+ \label{eq:regular-continuant-layer}
+\end{equation}
+
+We first evaluate the context mass.  Canonical words in
+\(\mathcal C_{\rm R}\) with
+denominator \(q\) parameterize the \(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in
+\((0,1)\).  Hence, for \(s>2\),
+\begin{equation}
+ R_s:=\sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}\mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s}
+ =1+\sum_{q\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(q)}{q^s}
+ =\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}<\infty.
+ \label{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}
+\end{equation}
+Every nonempty positive word either ends in a digit at least two or has the
+form \((a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)\).  The usual terminal move
+\[
+ (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)
+ \longleftrightarrow
+ (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1}+1)
+\]
+preserves the continuant.  It pairs the two regular expansions of every
+nonempty canonical word; it also pairs \((1)\) with \(\varnothing\).  Therefore
+\begin{equation}
+ L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}\mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+ =2R_s.
+ \label{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}
+\end{equation}
+This proves the absolute convergence and the evaluation in
+\eqref{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}.
+
+It remains to prove that this context sum is the whole local main term.  We
+give the cutoff argument, including the multiple-large-digit and moderate
+parts.  The continuant concatenation formula implies, for finite positive
+words \(\mathbf u,\mathbf v\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u\mathbf v)
+ \ge \mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v).
+ \label{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound}
+\end{equation}
+Moreover, with the two contexts fixed and \(a\to\infty\), multilinearity of
+the tridiagonal determinant defining the continuant gives
+\begin{equation}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)
+ =a\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)+O_{\mathbf u,\mathbf v}(1).
+ \label{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine}
+\end{equation}
+
+Let \(P_n(s)\) be the part of \eqref{eq:regular-continuant-layer} coming from
+words having a digit greater than \(n/2\).  Such a digit is unique.  Cutting
+there is a bijection with pairs
+\((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\times\mathcal C_{\rm R}\)
+satisfying
+\(|\mathbf u|_1+|\mathbf v|_1<n/2\), the middle digit being
+\(a=n-|\mathbf u|_1-|\mathbf v|_1\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} and
+\eqref{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine} give, respectively,
+\[
+ n^s\mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)^{-s}
+ \le 2^s\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}
+\]
+and pointwise convergence of the left side to
+\(\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\).  Dominated
+convergence, using \eqref{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}--
+\eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, therefore yields
+\begin{equation}
+ n^sP_n(s)\longrightarrow L_sR_s=b(s).
+ \label{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}
+\end{equation}
+
+We now show that the complementary words have total weight \(o(n^{-s})\).
+Choose
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{s}{2(s-1)}<\delta<1,
+ \qquad h=\lfloor n^\delta\rfloor,
+ \label{eq:large-digit-cutoff}
+\end{equation}
+and set
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+By \eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).  A word having
+at least two digits not smaller than \(h\) can be cut at its first two such
+digits.  After dropping the restrictions on the three intervening contexts,
+\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} bounds its total weight by
+\begin{equation}
+ L_s^2R_s
+ \left(\sum_{a\ge h}a^{-s}\right)^2
+ =O_s(h^{2-2s})=o(n^{-s}),
+ \label{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}
+\end{equation}
+where the last equality is precisely the first inequality in
+\eqref{eq:large-digit-cutoff}.
+
+For completeness, consider a word all of whose digits are smaller than
+\(h\).  Greedily divide it into consecutive blocks: close a block as soon as
+its digit sum reaches \(h\), and leave the last remainder unclosed.  Every
+closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum at least
+\(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.  The
+concatenation bound and the uniqueness of the greedy decomposition show that
+the total continuant weight of all such words is at most
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1}
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+for all sufficiently large \(h\).  When \(N\ge n/4\), this is
+\(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A>0\), because \(n/h\to\infty\) and
+\(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+
+The words not counted by \(P_n(s)\) and not covered by
+\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible} have at most one digit at least \(h\).
+If there is none, apply \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} with \(N=n\).  If
+there is exactly one, its value is at most \(n/2\), so the two surrounding
+moderate contexts have combined digit sum at least \(n/2\); one has digit sum
+at least \(n/4\).  Cutting at the exceptional digit, summing its weight
+\(a^{-s}\), and applying \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} to that long context
+again gives \(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A\).  Together with
+\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}, this proves
+\[
+ A_n(s)-P_n(s)=o(n^{-s}).
+\]
+Combining this with \eqref{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}, and replacing
+\(n=d+1\) by \(d\), proves \eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic critical stable renewal]
+\label{thm:arithmetic-critical-stable-renewal}
+Put \(\alpha:=\sigma_0-1\in(1,2)\), and under the critical letter law put
+\[
+ \Pr\{(C,H)=(c(p/q),\log q)\}=q^{-\sigma_0}.
+\]
+Then \(\Pr\{C=2d+1\}=b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)\), and the explicit constants
+\begin{equation}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ b_C&:=
+ \sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}
+ \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-\sigma_0}
+ =2\left(\frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}\right)^2=8,\\
+ K_C&:=\frac{2^{\sigma_0-1}}{\sigma_0-1}b_C
+ =\frac{2^{\sigma_0+2}}{\sigma_0-1}
+ \end{aligned}
+ \label{eq:critical-tail-constants}
+\end{equation}
+are positive.  The double series defining \(b_C\) is absolutely convergent,
+and
+\begin{align}
+ b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)&\sim b_Cd^{-\sigma_0},
+ &&d\to\infty,
+ \label{eq:critical-letter-local-tail}\\
+ \Pr\{C>x\}
+ &=\sum_{q\ge2}q^{-\sigma_0}
+   \card{\{1\le p<q:(p,q)=1,\ c(p/q)>x\}},\notag\\
+ &\sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0},
+ &&x\to\infty.
+ \label{eq:critical-letter-tail}
+\end{align}
+If \(u_j=u_j(\sigma_0)\) is the renewal sequence in
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-coefficients}, then
+\begin{equation}
+ u_j=\frac1{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)}j^{2-\sigma_0}
+ +o(j^{2-\sigma_0}).
+ \label{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}
+\end{equation}
+Consequently,
+\begin{align}
+ Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)
+ &=\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
+   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order}\\
+ S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
+ &=\frac{4m}{\mu_C}
+ +\frac{4K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
+   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}).
+ \label{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}
+\end{align}
+Finally, \(C\) belongs to the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive
+\(\alpha\)-stable law.  More precisely, if \(a_n>0\) is chosen so that
+\(n\Pr\{C>a_n\}\to1\), then for independent copies \(C_1,C_2,\ldots\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \frac{C_1+\cdots+C_n-n\mu_C}{a_n}
+ \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\mathcal S_\alpha,
+ \label{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}
+\end{equation}
+where \(\mathcal S_\alpha\) is the spectrally positive \(\alpha\)-stable law
+whose L\'evy measure has density \(\alpha x^{-\alpha-1}\) on \((0,\infty)\).
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The critical equation \eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} makes the displayed
+letter law a probability measure.  The local estimate
+\eqref{eq:critical-letter-local-tail} and the context-sum evaluation in
+\eqref{eq:critical-tail-constants} are \Cref{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
+at \(s=\sigma_0\).  Direct summation of that local estimate gives
+\[
+ \Pr\{C>x\}
+ =\sum_{d>(x-1)/2}b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)
+ \sim\frac{b_C}{\sigma_0-1}
+      \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^{1-\sigma_0},
+\]
+which is \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail} with the stated \(K_C\).  Thus
+regular variation is a conclusion of the arithmetic continuant estimate, not
+an assumption.
+
+The distribution of \(C\) has span one, finite mean \(\mu_C\), and tail
+\(K_Cj^{-\alpha}\), with \(1<\alpha<2\).  The finite-mean case of the
+discrete renewal-sequence theorem \cite{OmeyVanGulck2015} therefore gives
+\[
+ u_j-\frac1{\mu_C}
+ \sim\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\alpha-1)}j^{1-\alpha};
+\]
+the same coefficient also follows from the generating-function remainder
+argument for the arithmetic renewal theorem in \cite[Ch.~XI]{Feller1971}.
+Substitution of
+\(\alpha=\sigma_0-1\) proves
+\eqref{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}.  Summing it and using
+\[
+ \sum_{j=1}^{m-1}j^{2-\sigma_0}
+ \sim\frac{m^{3-\sigma_0}}{3-\sigma_0}
+\]
+in the exact identities \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-window-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order} and
+\eqref{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}; the boundary terms are
+\(O(1)=o(m^{3-\sigma_0})\).
+
+Finally, \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail}, finite mean, and the absence of a
+negative tail are precisely the one-sided domain-of-attraction conditions for
+an \(\alpha\)-stable law with the normalization in
+\eqref{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}; see \cite[Ch.~XVII]{Feller1971}.
+\end{proof}

# Arithmetic Criticality and Large Deviations for Fibonacci Partitions and Finite-Window Fibers

This directory contains the main manuscript `Arithmetic Criticality and Large
Deviations for Fibonacci Partitions and Finite-Window Fibers` and a separately
compiled supplement. The submission target is the *Journal of Number Theory*.

## Scope

The finite Fibonacci representation frequencies of Sidorov--Vershik are the
subset-sum coefficients used here after the exact shift
\(F_j^{\mathrm{SV}}=F_{j+1}\). With the convention for the golden-ratio
Bernoulli convolution used in the paper, the pressure dictionary is

\[
P(t)=t\log 2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi.
\]

The positive spectrum is attributed to Lau--Ngai, and the all-real spectrum
and negative first-order phase transition are attributed to Feng--Olivier and
Feng; Hu is cited for the early local-dimension theory. The all-real pressure
and frozen branch are recorded as finite-layer recovery and consistency
results.

The main contribution consists of:

- the exact indexing and normalization dictionary from the golden-ratio
  Bernoulli-convolution \(L^q\)-spectrum to Fibonacci partition layers;
- the arithmetic critical point, critical Gibbs law, and full finite-layer
  LDP on a single standard Fibonacci partition layer;
- the joint generation-cost and log-multiplicity LDP, including its affine
  two-dimensional coexistence face;
- the residue and affine fiber correspondence;
- the pointwise Fibonacci partition-difference formula;
- the exact two-layer interval identity and transferred extremal theorem;
- the uniform Weinstein layer-count lemma and the finite-layer recovery of the
  known negative-temperature frozen branch;
- the linear critical finite-size law and uniform critical coexistence limit;
- the full real-tilt large deviation principle across the freezing corner;
- the exact finite-prime-support coefficient interface and the explicit
  heavy-cost obstruction at the active cutoff.

The conditional microcanonical refinements, exact dyadic ray, integer moment
transfer, direct quadratic recurrence, and high-tilt consequences are in
`supplement.pdf`, not in the main theorem spine.

The fixed finite-prime-support result is an exact rational generating-function
interface only. No directional coefficient asymptotic or quenched-velocity
law is asserted.

The affine fiber--partition correspondence is stated for \(m\ge1\). In the
generic maximizing-residue formulas, \(I_{2k+1}\) is defined for \(k\ge5\),
whereas \(I_{2k}\) and \(J_{2k}\) are defined for \(k\ge7\); exceptional
initial cases are listed separately.

## Build

The bibliography is written directly in `sec_references.tex`; BibTeX is not
used. Compile the main article before the supplement so `xr-hyper` can resolve
cross-document references:

```powershell
latexmk -pdfxe -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex
latexmk -pdfxe -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error supplement.tex
```

The expected outputs are `main.pdf` and `supplement.pdf`.

# Submission Metadata

## Journal

Journal of Number Theory

## Title

Arithmetic Criticality and Large Deviations for Fibonacci Partitions and
Finite-Window Fibers

## Authors

- Haobo Ma, AELF PTE LTD., Singapore
- Wenlin Zhang, National University of Singapore, Singapore

## 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification

11B39, 05A17, 60F10

## Keywords

Fibonacci partition function; Erdos measure; Bernoulli convolution;
Zeckendorf representation; large deviations

## Summary

The manuscript studies the Fibonacci partition function and an exact
finite-window Zeckendorf fold. It identifies the arithmetic critical parameter
by

\[
\frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}=2,
\]

derives the critical finite-size constants \(2/\mu_C\) and \(4/\mu_C\),
proves uniform coexistence limits and finite-layer large deviations at
nonexposed slopes, and establishes exact finite-window fiber identities. On
each fixed finite prime support it retains an exact rational coefficient
generating function. It asserts no directional coefficient asymptotic and no
quenched-velocity asymptotic.

## Relation To Prior Results

Sidorov and Vershik use \(F^{\mathrm{SV}}_1=1\) and
\(F^{\mathrm{SV}}_2=2\), so their indexing is

\[
F^{\mathrm{SV}}_j=F_{j+1}.
\]

Their finite representation frequency \(f_m(k)\) is therefore the same raw
finite Fibonacci subset-sum coefficient used in the manuscript, after this
index shift, and \(2^{-m}f_m(k)\) gives the finite masses approximating the
Erdos measure. Hu treated local dimensions of the golden-ratio Bernoulli
convolution. Lau and Ngai determined its positive-\(q\) \(L^q\)-spectrum.
Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative
first-order phase transition.

With

\[
\tau_\mu(t)=\lim\frac{\log\sum_I\mu(I)^t}{\log|I|},
\]

the exact normalization used throughout the submission is

\[
P(t)=t\log 2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi.
\]

Accordingly, the all-real pressure formula and the frozen negative branch are
recorded as attributed recovery and consistency results. The surviving
contributions are the arithmetic evaluation of the critical point, the
one-sided critical moment, the critical finite-size constants and coexistence
laws, the finite-layer nonexposed-slope lower bounds, and the exact
finite-window correspondences and identities.

## Exact Scope Of Finite Formulas

The affine fiber--partition correspondence and partition-difference formula
hold for every integer \(m\ge 1\). The two-interval fiber identity itself is
stated for \(m\ge 0\).

For the maximizing-residue formulas, write \(G_j=F_{j+1}\). The odd-index
quantity

\[
I_{2k+1}=
\begin{cases}
G_{k+1}G_{k-3}+1,&k\text{ even},\\
G_kG_{k-2}+1,&k\text{ odd}
\end{cases}
\]

is defined only for \(k\ge 5\). The even-index quantities

\[
I_{2k}=
\begin{cases}
G_{k+2}G_{k-5}+G_3+1,&k\text{ even},\\
G_{k+1}G_{k-4}+G_3+1,&k\text{ odd}
\end{cases}
\]

and

\[
J_{2k}=
\begin{cases}
G_{k+1}G_{k-3}+1,&k\text{ even},\\
G_kG_{k-2}+1,&k\text{ odd}
\end{cases}
\]

are defined only for \(k\ge 7\). The exceptional initial maximizing residues
are listed separately in the manuscript and are not obtained by extending
these generic formulas below their stated ranges.

The largest-fiber values have their own ranges:

\[
D_0=D_1=1,\qquad D_{2k}=F_{k+2}\quad(k\ge0),\qquad
D_{2k+1}=2F_{k+1}\quad(k\ge1),
\]

and the recurrence \(D_m=D_{m-2}+D_{m-4}\) holds for \(m\ge6\).

## Submission Files

- `main.tex` and its section inputs: main article
- `supplement.tex`: separately compiled supplement
- `sec_references.tex`: manually maintained bibliography; BibTeX is not used
- Journal of Number Theory cover letter

The Editors
Journal of Number Theory

Dear Editors,

We submit for your consideration the manuscript "Arithmetic Criticality and
Large Deviations for Fibonacci Partitions and Finite-Window Fibers."

The paper studies the classical Fibonacci partition function R(n) and an exact
finite-window Zeckendorf fold. Its number-theoretic contributions are an
arithmetic evaluation of the critical parameter by
zeta(sigma_0-1)/zeta(sigma_0)=2, the critical finite-size constants
2/mu_C and 4/mu_C, uniform coexistence laws, finite-layer large deviations at
the nonexposed slopes, and exact finite-window fiber identities.

The pressure framework is attributed directly to the existing theory of the
Erdos measure and the golden-ratio Bernoulli convolution. Sidorov and Vershik's
finite representation frequencies use F_j^(SV)=F_{j+1} in our convention and
are exactly the raw subset-sum coefficients. Hu studied local dimensions,
Lau and Ngai determined the positive-q L^q-spectrum, and Feng--Olivier and
Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative first-order phase
transition. In our convention the normalization is

    P(t) = t log 2 - tau_mu(t) log phi.

Accordingly, the manuscript records the all-real pressure and frozen branch as
recovery and consistency results. It does not claim them as new. A
theorem-by-theorem table in the introduction separates every imported result,
normalization, and surviving contribution.

The finite identities are stated with their exact domains. The affine
fiber--partition correspondence holds for m >= 1. In the maximizing-residue
formulas, I_{2k+1} is defined for k >= 5, while I_{2k} and J_{2k} are defined
for k >= 7. The manuscript also retains an exact rational generating-function
interface on each fixed finite prime support, but asserts no directional
coefficient or quenched-velocity asymptotic.

The main article is in amsart format. A separately compiled supplement contains
conditional arithmetic and integer-moment consequences. All external inputs,
including the extremal classification of Kocabova--Masakova--Pelantova,
Weinstein's free-generator decomposition, Stern--Brocot denominator pressure,
and standard renewal, Tauberian, and large-deviation theorems, are identified
at their points of use.

Thank you for considering this submission.

Sincerely,
The Authors
